html:
Haiti is the country on the western third of the island of Hispaniola in the Caribbean. It was born in 1804 from the only slave revolt in history that founded a state.

Spain ceded this part of the island to France in 1697. As the French colony of Saint-Domingue it became the richest colony in the world, growing sugar and coffee with hundreds of thousands of Africans brought through the Atlantic slave trade. The great revolt of 1791 grew into a war led by Toussaint Louverture against France, Spain and Britain. Jean-Jacques Dessalines declared independence on 1 January 1804.

The new state paid dearly for its freedom:

  • In 1825 France demanded a huge indemnity, backed by warships, as the price of recognition. Haiti paid it for decades.
  • The country split for a time into a northern kingdom and a southern republic, then ruled the whole island from 1822 to 1844, when the Dominican Republic broke away.
  • The United States occupied Haiti from 1915 to 1934.
  • François Duvalier and then his son ruled as dictators from 1957 to 1986, using the Tonton Macoute militia.

Since then Haiti has seen elections, coups and foreign missions. The earthquake of 2010 destroyed much of Port-au-Prince and killed a vast number of people. Haitian Creole and French are its languages, and Vodou and Catholicism its main faiths.
sum: Haiti is the country on the western third of the island of Hispaniola in the Caribbean. It was born in 1804 from the only slave revolt in history that founded a state.
